findings.description: The bucket is explicitly noted as public with no ACL restricting access, allowing anyone to read or write objects including sensitive data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, so objects can be overwritten or deleted without the ability to recover prior versions, increasing risk from accidental or malicious data loss/tampering.
No logging block is configured, meaning access to this bucket (which is public and unencrypted) cannot be audited.
A sensitive file (customer-master.xlsx, likely containing customer PII) is uploaded to the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is public and unencrypted, exposing customer data to anyone.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket storing financial data, leaving it unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled for this financial data bucket, risking irreversible data loss or tampering.
No logging configuration exists for this bucket, preventing audit of access to financial data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operational data stored here is not encrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, preventing audit trails of access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so data science bucket contents are unencrypted at rest.
